paragraphs.text: Fausto Elizondo Marroquín participated in Seizure PRS-11-02 on 2011-12-12. Círculo del Valle Quieto was linked to Seizure PRS-11-02 on 2011-12-12. Seizure PRS-11-02 occurred at Presidio on 2011-12-12. A used car exporter in Calexico with business contacts in the Chihuahua trucking trade reported that inspectors at the Presidio port of entry recovered 45 kg of methamphetamine from the light aircraft the crews call Avioneta Jade Marino after it was trailered across the bridge as cargo under paperwork from Autotransportes Sierra Madre Norte. The exporter attributed the load to Elizondo, the trucking logistics figure for Círculo del Valle Quieto known as El Capataz.

Autotransportes Sierra Madre Norte supported Seizure PRS-11-02 on 2011-12-12. Avioneta Jade Marino was involved in Seizure PRS-11-02 on 2011-12-12. Seizure PRS-11-02 transited Ojinaga crossing on 2011-12-12. The exporter stated that the aircraft was declared as a disassembled airframe for repair and that the methamphetamine was packed inside the wing roots. The exporter characterized the use of the Ojinaga crossing as a test of a quieter route after losses on the Tamaulipas bridges.

Círculo del Valle Quieto controlled Ojinaga crossing from 2010-09-01 until 2020-05-15. Aurelio Castañón Vidaurri led Círculo del Valle Quieto from 2010-09-01 until 2019-05-23. Fausto Elizondo Marroquín was a member of Círculo del Valle Quieto from 2010-09-01 until 2027-01-01. The exporter described the Ojinaga crossing as under the network's control through local arrangements and Castañón as the head of the network. Elizondo was described as a founding member who owns the trucking firm on the network's behalf.

Fausto Elizondo Marroquín owned Autotransportes Sierra Madre Norte on 2010-10-01. Cristóbal Arizpe Dávalos was the nominee owner of Autotransportes Sierra Madre Norte on 2010-10-01. The exporter stated that the firm's registration lists Elizondo as owner and the lawyer Arizpe, called El Perito, as a nominee, and that the firm's export paperwork is prepared in Arizpe's office. The reporting office assesses the exporter as having secondhand access through trade contacts and notes that the company registration was confirmed against registry extracts. The quantity reported here was taken from the exporter's contact and has not been verified against the seizure record.
